quarterly_data.signal: FIRST-QUARTER RESULTS BEAT, DRIVEN BY DATA-CENTER USAGE. CFO David Poroch: first quarter 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.32 per share, $0.09 higher than the first quarter of 2025 and $0.12 above the company's estimate. Primary drivers were meaningful customer growth and increased usage, including from data centers at the state-regulated electric utilities, plus higher gas-utility revenues and higher energy-related revenues at Southern Power, partly offset by higher financing costs and milder weather. Adjusted EPS estimate for the second quarter is $1.00 per share.
quarterly_data.figure: Adjusted EPS $1.32 ($0.09 higher YoY, $0.12 above estimate); second-quarter adjusted EPS estimate $1.00

quarterly_data.signal: CONTRACTED LARGE LOAD PASSES 11 GW. CEO Chris Womack: in just the last two months the company signed contracts for another 1.9 GW of customer load with high credit quality hyperscalers (Poroch: Georgia Power signed two projects representing 1.9 GW), bringing fully contracted large-load agreements to more than 11 GW across Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi. Demand across the electric territories has culminated in 23 GW of contracted or late-stage load. The bilaterally negotiated agreements are structured so that customers driving incremental demand cover the full share of the cost to serve them.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.9 GW newly contracted with hyperscalers in two months; over 11 GW contracted large load; 23 GW contracted or late-stage

quarterly_data.signal: LATE-STAGE PIPELINE GROWS TO 12 GW; PROSPECTIVE PIPELINE WELL OVER 75 GW. Poroch: interest from large load customers (data centers and large manufacturers) remains strong with a prospective pipeline of well over 75 GW. The company is in active late-stage discussions for another 12 GW of contracted load through the mid-2030s, an increase of 2 GW from last quarter, and roughly 6 GW or half of those late-stage gigawatts are expected to be finalized with executed contracts in the near term. In a little over two months, projects representing 12 GW advanced to the next stage. Womack said activity is migrating west, with greater activity in Alabama and Mississippi while Georgia remains very strong, and noted 'repeat buyers' coming back for more capacity; Poroch said Georgia's collateral requirement is shaking out speculative projects.
quarterly_data.figure: Prospective pipeline well over 75 GW; late-stage 12 GW (+2 GW vs last quarter); roughly 6 GW expected to be contracted near term

quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER USAGE UP 42% YEAR OVER YEAR. Poroch: first-quarter weather-normal retail electricity sales to all classes were 2.3% higher than the first quarter of 2025, the highest first-quarter total retail sales growth in recent history. The commercial class grew 4.5% weather-adjusted, bolstered by data centers; data center usage was up 42% year-over-year, primarily due to accelerating usage ramps at large load facilities. Industrial sales grew 1.5% and 46,000 new residential customers were added.
quarterly_data.figure: Weather-normal retail sales +2.3%; commercial +4.5%; data center usage +42% YoY; industrial +1.5%; 46,000 new residential customers

quarterly_data.signal: GENERATION BUILD FOR LOAD GROWTH: FIRST 10 GW ASSETS ONLINE AND NEW 2-6 GW GEORGIA RFP. Womack: Georgia Power achieved commercial operation of two battery energy storage systems providing nearly 200 MW, the first of the 10 GW portfolio of approved new generation (including battery systems and natural gas combustion turbines projected online later in 2026 and 2027). Poroch: Georgia Power initiated the regulatory process for an all-source RFP to procure 2-6 GW of new dispatchable generation for in-service in 2032 and 2033; company-owned resources selected in the Alabama Power and Georgia Power RFPs would be substantial incremental investment above the base capital plan. Timeline: selection through the rest of this year, certification pretty much through 2027, spend likely initiating in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Two battery systems, nearly 200 MW online; 10 GW approved generation portfolio; Georgia all-source RFP for 2-6 GW in service 2032 and 2033

quarterly_data.signal: SOUTHERN POWER GAS-TURBINE UPRATES. Poroch: Southern Power is moving forward with 400 MW of additional capacity through natural gas turbine upgrades at multiple existing facilities in Alabama and Georgia, with commercial operation projected between 2029 and 2031, adding approximately $700 million to the capital plan; an additional 300 MW of natural gas uprates is under evaluation (covering the whole fleet; timing probably over the course of the next year or so). Contracting for the 400 MW is in fairly late-stage conversations; Womack said Southern Power has said numbers 'up in the mid-90s in terms of what's contracted' and that recontracting talks and conversations with potential hyperscalers are both underway. 'we don't take merchant risk.'
quarterly_data.figure: 400 MW uprates, commercial operation between 2029 and 2031, approximately $700 million capex; additional 300 MW under evaluation

quarterly_data.signal: FINANCING THE BUILDOUT: DOE LOANS AND REMAINING EQUITY NEED. Womack highlighted $26.5 billion in loan agreements with the Department of Energy benefiting Alabama and Georgia customers, projected to generate cumulative customer savings of $7 billion over the approximately 30-year term. Poroch: an incremental $500 million of equity was sourced through the ATM program; including the $700 million of Southern Power capex, the remaining need for equity or equity equivalents is approximately $1.8 billion through 2030, on a path to 17% FFO to debt by 2029; incremental capital is expected to be funded about 40% with equity.
quarterly_data.figure: $26.5 billion DOE loans ($7 billion projected customer savings); $500 million ATM equity; remaining equity need approximately $1.8 billion through 2030

quarterly_data.signal: SUPPLY CHAIN FOR THE BUILDOUT - TURBINES, TRANSFORMERS, CABLE AND LABOR. Asked about tight areas, Womack said 'it's not anything you can take for granted' but the headline is the company is 'very well positioned' thanks to its scale and long supplier relationships, and must keep working it 'whether it's turbines, whether it's transformers, whether it's hot wire, cable, name it.' The company has the turbines identified to support its RFPs and holds positions with turbine suppliers and OEMs on both delivery and pricing. He expects some tightness in the labor market and cited some 10,000 laborers at peak on the Vogtle construction as the basis of its labor relationships.
